title: Frobenius/Zolotarev for squarefree odd n: sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/n) = J(a | n)

insights: The general odd-squarefree statement is the recursive structure of the Jacobi symbol made structural: jacobiSym.mul_right (denominator multiplicativity of the symbol) is the value-level shadow of the grandparent's sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd (CRT multiplicativity of the permutation sign), and the recursion bottoms out at the parent's prime base case.

Squarefreeness is exactly the hypothesis that makes the smallest prime factor split off coprimely: p ∣ (n/p) would give p² ∣ n, so Squarefree n forces Coprime p (n/p) — the input sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd needs at every recursion step.

Representing the unit by the integer a makes the Chinese-remainder component-matching automatic: the projection of (a : ℤ/n) onto ℤ/p is (a : ℤ/p) by map_intCast, so no residue bookkeeping is needed (simp [map_intCast] closes the matching hypotheses).
Manufacturing the per-prime component units costs only a one-line Bezout bridge (intCast_isUnit_of_isCoprime): x·a + y·k = 1 reduces mod k to x·a = 1.

Strong induction (Nat.strong_induction_on) on the bare n, with the [NeZero n] instance placed inside the quantified motive, avoids instance-revert problems; the n = 1 base uses the subsingleton structure of ℤ/1.
